*Dutiyaoguṇṭhita* ("Covering the head", Sekhiya 24) is a training rule (*sekhiya-dhamma*) preserved in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text concerns monastic deportment, specifically the second rule concerning covering the head while moving or sitting in inhabited areas. It has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral show extensive transmission of this rule across Vinaya traditions, including the Theravāda Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bu-pm-sk24*), the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra, and the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (*pli-tv-bi-vb-sk24*) and Pātimokkha, as well as Chinese and Sanskrit Vinaya lineages belonging to the Sarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Dharmaguptaka, Mahāsāṅghika, and Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda schools [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus computes 109 internal Pali reuse passages across 50 texts, reflecting the highly standardized framing of the Sekhiya section, with extensive shared text in segments §0.1–1.15 occurring in adjacent rules such as Sekhiya 22, Sekhiya 18, and Sekhiya 20 [DharmaNexus]. Occurrences of the abbreviation "SK 24" in surveyed secondary philosophical literature refer exclusively to the *Sāṃkhyakārikā* rather than this Vinaya rule.
